name: Empire State Building
ranking: #11 of 2,861 things to do in New York City
description: We asked travelers around the globe what place wowed them most, and they pointed straight up: 1,454 feet up, to be exact. Yes, the Empire State Building won our Travelers’ Choice Award as the top attraction in the world. Even jaded New Yorkers get a rush of affection seeing its sleek, symmetrical facade. With stainless-steel canopies, black granite detailing, molded eagles, and that iconic spire antenna, it’s a full-on Art Deco masterpiece. No wonder King Kong wanted to hang here. And sure, it’s no longer the tallest building in the city (it’s topped by seven others these days), but it’s got plenty of glamour to spare. While the ESB is technically a functioning office building, there’s still plenty for visitors to see. For starters: those views. You can get ‘em from two vantage points: an open-air observatory on the 86th floor and an indoor one on the 102nd floor. There’s also a second-floor museum and exhibits on the 80th floor. But even if you don't make it inside, you can see its famous lights from all over the city. They change for different occasions; say, orange for a Knicks home game or, yes, even “Tripadvisor green” for that Travelers’ Choice win.
